# Debian Forky unattended-installation code audit - second pass

**Audit date:** 16 October 2026. **Target contract:** Debian Forky with systemd 262, as specified by the requester. **Deliverable:** source audit, implementation analysis and narrowly scoped recommendations. No source, service, configuration, package, runtime or Xwayland changes were made; no software was compiled.

**Contents:** [Assessment](#section-1) | [Scope and evidence](#section-2) | [13 findings](#section-3) | [19 component audits](#section-4) | [Improvement register](#section-5) | [Remediation ownership](#section-6) | [Acceptance matrix](#section-7) | [374 primary file records](#section-8) | [Supporting-source register](#section-9) | [Verification limits](#section-10) | [Upstream contracts](#section-11) | [21 second-pass boundary reviews](#section-12) | [83 delegated Python files](#section-13) | [systemd contract inventory](#section-14)

<a id="section-1"></a>
## 1. Executive assessment

The implementation already contains substantial security controls: explicit privileged dispatch, private and validated workspaces, namespace descriptor checks, application network leases, bounded process runners, constrained AppArmor rule rendering, signed local APT metadata, recovery-aware storage workflows and dedicated lifecycle owners. The appropriate response is to correct the identified defects locally while retaining those controls, not to replace the architecture or conduct unrelated hardening changes.

**13 concrete findings: 3 High, 8 Medium and 2 Low.** The highest-impact findings concern AppArmor mode transitions loading stale child-policy flags, new llama/Whisper downloads rejecting their own staging filenames, and Samsung flashing losing its association with the selected device during the protocol transition. The other findings cover filesystem error guards, recovery-backup retention, concurrent pruning, extraction budgets, PDF processing, persistent firewall recovery, recording status, SSH operands and a privileged process-cleanup identity race identified in this second pass.

The affected device-flashing path should fail closed until device identity can be maintained. New-model installation requires a local staging/final-name correction; existing installed models follow a separate branch. AppArmor filesystem guards, transition ordering and recovery retention need cohesive but narrow fixes. None of these findings justifies weakening policy checks, broadening the private compatibility boundary or adding source-built replacements.

Severity describes operational impact, not CVSS. **High** denotes materially incorrect security state, unavailable principal functionality or credible risk of an irreversible action against the wrong target. **Medium** denotes a meaningful bounded integrity, availability, confidentiality or recovery defect. **Low** denotes localized correctness or defence-in-depth defects. A source-level race or contract failure is identified as such; no live exploit, successful install or target enforcement result is claimed.

<a id="section-2"></a>
## 2. Scope, evidence and assurance

### 2.1 Exact requested coverage

Every regular file present in the three requested executable trees and every requested Perl tree is included, recursively. Repeated AndroidADB/AppArmor listings are resolved to the actual directories. The Timeshift heading is treated as the complete supplied TimeshiftManaged package, not just its CLI. Nested firmware/vendor, Zram and `libexec/timeshift` directories are included.

The exact requested trees contain **373 files and 84,035 physical lines**. The adjacent Zram package loader, `d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/zram-writeback/Zram.pm`, contributes **one additional entry-boundary file and 12 lines**. Accordingly, the primary file-by-file register contains **374 records and 84,047 lines**. No requested regular file is missing from that register.

The review follows wrappers into their real implementations: **75 Python files/templates under the installed `python3.14/dist-packages` tree and eight hardware-tuning modules**, totalling **83 delegated implementation files and 22,041 lines**, receive a separate complete source register. Installation scripts, systemd units/drop-ins, AppArmor policies, polkit rules, sudoers, configuration, desktop entries and relevant tests are represented in the supporting-source register. Section 14 separately inventories current installed systemd configuration and generated Podman unit templates.

### 2.2 What the second pass actually did

The ZIP was safely extracted to a separate workspace with canonical containment and member-type checks. The review indexed paths, source hashes, definitions, imports, call/delegation references, security-sensitive operations and declarative unit contracts. It compared requested scope against the individual file register and rechecked finding control flow, ownership transitions, error/cleanup behaviour and applicable primary upstream command contracts. It added the detailed boundary analyses in section 12 and the delegated implementation/unit inventories in sections 13-14.

**Completed parser-only checks:** 414 Python source/template files parsed successfully as data; 296 shell source/template files passed the applicable shell's `-n` parser-only check. No repository Python or Perl module was imported. Shell parsing did not execute the scripts. These checks cover a broader archive set than the primary scope and are not dependency, type, rendered-template, service-start or functional results.

No repository test runner, helper, installer, management command, network operation, firmware command, storage operation, TPM/enrollment operation or service was executed. No target behaviour was inferred from the audit host's kernel or service manager. Existing tests and historical validation material were read as source evidence only. This follows the supplied repository's isolation requirements in `AGENTS.override.md`.

### 2.3 What complete coverage means here

Every primary file has an identifiable source record, responsibility, implementation-symbol inventory, caller/delegate information, review disposition, improvement rationale and acceptance target. The Python and systemd inventories make transitive coverage explicit instead of treating a short wrapper as the whole implementation. The 19 component chapters and 21 second-pass reviews explain the relevant input, authority, execution, persistence and cleanup boundaries.

Review depth is risk-based. File accounting and parser success do not mean every branch was dynamically executed or formally proved safe. Named-symbol and literal-reference indexes can omit anonymous closures, generated names and dynamic dispatch; zero indexed references do not prove dead code. No claim of universal absence of vulnerabilities or complete target compatibility is made. Required but unexecuted target checks are clearly separated from completed static work.

### 2.4 Trust boundaries and preservation constraints

The principal boundaries are user/menu to privileged action; interpreter bootstrap to installed delegate; client to network-namespace broker; external artifact to parser/publisher; document/archive to transformation process; policy source to loaded enforcement; launcher to transient service descendants; device selection to destructive operation; and saved recovery state to a subsequent boot.

Same-UID state is not a root authorization boundary. A path allowlist does not prove ownership; an atomic file replacement is not a multi-file transaction; process-group cleanup is not cgroup containment; a socket listening is not full protocol readiness; and a digest only authenticates bytes relative to a trusted expected value. These distinctions are applied to concrete paths rather than used to generate speculative findings.

The existing private Xwayland boundary remains exclusively Zoom and Discord. The audit neither modifies it nor recommends a global Xwayland fallback, another eligible application, a new runtime build or changes to its current implementation. All recommendations use existing architecture and packaged capabilities unless a narrowly scoped correction is explicitly described.

<a id="f01"></a>
### F01 - Perl list-operator precedence disables AppArmor filesystem error guards

**Severity:** Medium. **Classification:** Confirmed error-handling defect.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/Workspace.pm`](#file-235); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/TrustedPath.pm`](#file-233); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/Tool.pm`](#file-231); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/Transition.pm`](#file-232); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/LocalChildren.pm`](#file-229).

**Evidence and control flow:** Workspace.pm:79,101,103 uses chmod/rename ... || fatal without grouping; line104 forgets the staged path even if rename fails. Similar ungrouped sysopen/open/binmode/print/unlink/mkdir/symlink expressions occur in the other four modules. The documented Perl precedence places the fatal expression in the last argument rather than making it a guard on the syscall result. Unary close guards are not this defect. [S3]

**Impact and limits:** I/O, permission, publication, redirection and cleanup errors may be missed at their origin. Later source/kernel verification catches many resulting mismatches, so this is not proof of universal false-success or a privilege-escalation exploit. Optional label-less disable entries and cleanup errors can escape that later check.

**Narrow correction:** Change only affected list-operator guards to low-precedence or fatal(...) or explicitly parenthesize the operation. Preserve correctly grouped/unary guards; retain staging until successful publication. Add fixture-only failure injection for rename, open, symlink, print, chmod and unlink.

**Reason / benefit:** Filesystem failures surface at their origin, staging is not forgotten after failed publication, and recovery remains actionable.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Static source and the primary Perl operator-precedence contract; repository Perl modules and tests were not executed.

**Source excerpt - [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/Workspace.pm`](#file-235), L99-105:**

```text
  99      _copy_stream($source_fh, $target_fh, $message);
 100      close $source_fh || fatal($message);
 101      chmod 0644, $temporary_path || fatal($message);
 102      close $target_fh || fatal($message);
 103      rename $temporary_path, $target || fatal($message);
 104      delete $self->files()->{$temporary_path};
 105  }
```


<a id="f02"></a>
### F02 - Live AppArmor mode changes can load stale child-profile flags

**Severity:** High. **Classification:** Confirmed transition-order defect; target manifestation not executed.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/Transition.pm`](#file-232); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/apparmor-modes/AppArmor/ManagedModes/LocalChildren.pm`](#file-229); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/libexec/apparmor-modes-run`](#file-004).

**Evidence and control flow:** Transition.pm:150-154 symlinks the live local include directory into the staged tree; :170-173 runs aa-audit --remove with reload enabled by default; only :177 updates the tracked child includes; :186-190 publishes the parent. No subsequent parser reload occurs in this branch. LocalChildren.pm:21-25 identifies edge-glycin-bwrap, mullvad-bwrap and vivaldi-bwrap. apparmor-modes-run:88-94 then verifies source and kernel. [S4]

**Impact and limits:** Changing a tracked parent/child from complain to enforce or vice versa can load the new parent with old child mode. Final verification fails rather than repairing the mismatch; a second reconciliation is needed. Until then enforcement may be weaker than intended or dependent boot/session activation may fail. Does not affect unchanged modes or --no-reload staging in the same way.

**Narrow correction:** Keep aa-* source edits no-reload; stage and validate parent plus child changes, publish them, then invoke one explicit parser reload when reload_profiles is true and verify all labels. Preserve no-reload semantics and retain recoverable old bytes on failure. No policy broadening or Xwayland change.

**Reason / benefit:** A successful single transition means both parent and child source/loaded modes agree, rather than relying on a second repair run.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Source-order proof and official aa-audit documentation. Native nested-child kernel transition tests are required on the target and were not run.

<a id="f03"></a>
### F03 - Screen recording can report success status after producing an empty output

**Severity:** Low. **Classification:** Confirmed status-reporting defect.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/bin/labwc-capture.tmpl`](#file-149).

**Evidence and control flow:** record_worker:528-537 takes the failure branch for an empty output, removes it, emits an error notification, but exits with recording_status, which may be zero.

**Impact and limits:** systemd and callers can record a successful operation even though no recording exists. This is an observability/reliability issue, not an established privilege escalation.

**Narrow correction:** In the failed-artifact branch, map zero child status to a nonzero worker status; preserve nonzero child status and intentional-stop handling. Add a fixture recorder that exits zero without writing output.

**Reason / benefit:** Automation and service status agree with whether a usable recording was actually produced.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Static control-flow review; no desktop recording or session tests executed.

<a id="f04"></a>
### F04 - AppArmor rule generation removes its recovery backups even when rollback fails

**Severity:** Medium. **Classification:** Confirmed recovery defect on rollback failure.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/labwc-security-action/LabwcSecurityAction/AppArmor/RuleGenerator.pm.tmpl`](#file-300).

**Evidence and control flow:** RuleGenerator.pm.tmpl:230-247 stores prior include bytes in the batch directory. At :268-275, _rollback returns restoration/reload errors, but remove_tree($batch) runs unconditionally before reporting the warning. _rollback:675-699 can fail to restore published includes or reload their old profiles.

**Impact and limits:** A failed transaction can leave mixed policy state and delete the only transaction-local copies needed for manual recovery. The failure is reported; this is not a silent-success claim.

**Narrow correction:** Delete the batch only after complete successful rollback. On rollback error retain the root-private 0700 workspace, identify its path in the diagnostic, and preserve a bounded recovery record. Keep successful cleanup unchanged.

**Reason / benefit:** An administrator retains the exact pre-transaction policy bytes when automatic restoration cannot finish.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Static branch and workspace-lifetime review only; restoration failures were not induced on host policy.

**Source excerpt - [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/labwc-security-action/LabwcSecurityAction/AppArmor/RuleGenerator.pm.tmpl`](#file-300), L266-276:**

<a id="f05"></a>
### F05 - New llama and Whisper downloads are always rejected by final-name validation

**Severity:** High. **Classification:** Confirmed deterministic functional defect.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/ai-copilots/AICopilots/ModelInstallRoot.pm`](#file-221).

**Evidence and control flow:** _family_policy:54-73 accepts only final .gguf or ggml-*.bin basenames. _download:386-390 creates .<filename>.partial.<random>. At :424-430 it passes that partial to _validate_model, whose :324-325 applies the final-name expression. The leading dot and .partial suffix cannot match either expression. Cleanup at :453-456 removes the downloaded partial.

**Impact and limits:** Every new custom or catalog model download fails after transfer, regardless of valid content, digest or size. Existing final models use :372-381 and are not affected. This wastes potentially multi-gigabyte transfers; not a proven privilege-escalation issue.

**Narrow correction:** Separate trusted staging-path validation from final basename validation. Validate the requested final filename once, retain the exact tempfile handle/path as the staging identity, and apply canonical parent, owner, mode, size, magic and digest checks to both. Do not weaken the final filename allowlist or accept arbitrary partial paths.

**Reason / benefit:** Valid new models can be installed without weakening final-path, ownership, content or digest checks.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Static expression/argument-flow proof only. Add a disposable fixture performing full temporary creation, download stub, content verification and rename for both families; do not mock away _validate_model.

<a id="f06"></a>
### F06 - Model partial pruning does not coordinate with active per-model download locks

**Severity:** Medium. **Classification:** Confirmed concurrency defect.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/ai-copilots/AICopilots/ModelInstallRoot.pm`](#file-221).

**Evidence and control flow:** _download:371 holds .$filename.lock during transfer. _prune:479-500 iterates matching root-owned 0600 partials and unlinks them without acquiring the corresponding lock or checking age/ownership by an active download.

**Impact and limits:** An authorized prune operation racing an active download removes its pathname. The downloader then fails verification/publication, even after F05 is fixed. Not arbitrary-file deletion: the directory and name/mode constraints narrow the candidates.

**Narrow correction:** Derive the validated final filename from each candidate and take its existing per-model lock nonblocking before removal; skip busy downloads and restat under the lock. Apply the maximum-removal check before unlink rather than after removing entry 101.

**Reason / benefit:** Maintenance no longer destroys the pathname of an active download; one existing lock protocol defines ownership.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Static lock-scope comparison. Required fixture: hold model lock and partial, invoke prune, verify partial survives; release lock and verify eligible cleanup.


<a id="f07"></a>
### F07 - Generic repository extraction enforces aggregate limits only after expensive parsing/extraction

**Severity:** Medium. **Classification:** Confirmed resource-bound placement gap; no exploit executed.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/libexec/apt-repo-local`](#file-007); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/libexec/tuta-extract`](#file-119).

**Evidence and control flow:** apt-repo-local:1041-1056 calls tarfile.getmembers before its member-count check; :1059-1082 runs unsquashfs as the root publisher, with a timeout and per-file RLIMIT_FSIZE but no aggregate tree bound during extraction; :1085 onward first materializes rglob into a list before enforcing count. Tree byte/count checks in package assembly occur after writes. tuta-extract:95-120,170-205 provides an existing stricter unprivileged namespaced parser with CPU/address-space/file limits and a live tree watchdog.

**Impact and limits:** A corrupted or hostile accepted vendor artifact can consume disproportionate memory, disk/inodes or parser resources before rejection. Finite command timeouts and per-file limits reduce but do not bound aggregate expansion; no parser CVE or root-code-execution exploit is established.

**Narrow correction:** Reuse the existing packaged-parser isolation pattern without running AppImage runtimes or compiling tools. Stream tar membership/count accounting, check aggregate extraction growth while work is running, and iterate output paths incrementally. Keep package-specific limits and enforce disk/inode headroom; a watchdog is not a hard filesystem quota.

**Reason / benefit:** Malformed accepted artifacts cannot exhaust aggregate resources before a post-extraction limit finally notices them.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Static API/order review. Target-only fixture cases: excessive small members, large aggregate expansion, stalled parser, parser crash, cleanup on cancellation.


<a id="f08"></a>
### F08 - PDF encryption validation omits the password required to open the new file

**Severity:** Medium. **Classification:** Confirmed CLI contract defect; native qpdf not executed.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/digital-assets/DigitalAssets/PDF.pm`](#file-264); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/digital-assets/DigitalAssets/Context.pm.tmpl`](#file-259).

**Evidence and control flow:** PDF.pm:304-320 obtains nonempty user and owner passwords, writes qpdf encryption arguments privately, creates an encrypted output, then invokes qpdf --check output without --password-file. Context.pm.tmpl:334-338 requires at least eight characters; the empty-password exception does not apply. _run treats nonzero as fatal. [S5]

**Impact and limits:** Successful creation of a password-protected PDF is followed by an expected password error and an overall failed action, leaving a valid but unreported output.

**Narrow correction:** Create/reuse a private user-password file for the validation invocation and pass --password-file, keeping passwords out of argv and logs. Keep output verification and cleanup; do not suppress all qpdf errors.

**Reason / benefit:** Password-protected output is checked correctly without putting credentials into process arguments or diagnostics.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Source-flow review and official qpdf CLI password contract. Required target fixture: encrypt with two nonempty passwords, verify success with user password, failure without it, and no secret in captured argv/logs.

<a id="f09"></a>
### F09 - QDF repair output is sent to the terminal instead of the next pipeline input

**Severity:** Medium. **Classification:** Confirmed output-routing defect; native fix-qdf not executed.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/digital-assets/DigitalAssets/PDF.pm`](#file-264).

**Evidence and control flow:** PDF.pm:273 invokes fix-qdf with one input filename. Its documented contract sends repaired content to stdout unless an output filename is supplied. At :274 qpdf reads the original, still-unrepaired $qdf file. Context::run_timed does not redirect stdout. [S6]

**Impact and limits:** Length-changing edits can leave stale offsets/stream lengths and cause recovery warnings or failure; repaired, potentially sensitive uncompressed document content is also printed to terminal/output capture. Equal-length edits may appear to work, masking the defect.

**Narrow correction:** Pass a distinct private repaired output path to fix-qdf and feed that file into qpdf; validate the repaired artifact before final publication. Never redirect back over the input or suppress integrity warnings globally.

**Reason / benefit:** The next stage consumes repaired offsets/lengths, and private document contents do not spill to inherited stdout.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Source call arguments plus official fix-qdf input/output documentation. Required fixture: length-changing text edit, valid resulting PDF, and no document body on stdout.

```text
 274      $context->run_timed($qpdf, $qdf, $output);

```


<a id="f10"></a>
### F10 - Samsung flashing does not preserve the selected device identity across the ADB-to-download transition

**Severity:** High. **Classification:** Confirmed device-binding gap; destructive consequence is conditional and was not exercised.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/labwc-adb/AndroidADB/Vendor/Samsung.pm`](#file-287).

**Evidence and control flow:** Samsung.pm:229-285 validates the selected ADB serial/model and reboots that serial. At :400-426 the wait gate accepts a single Samsung download-mode USB device by vendor/product count only. At :288-309 the flash invocation uses samloader --usb-backend nusb flash --wait without a binding to the previously selected serial or physical USB attachment. labwc-adb-menu:556-581 and Validation.pm:448-464 provide explicit destructive confirmation, but do not bind the later USB transport.

**Impact and limits:** If another compatible Samsung device is already the only download-mode device while the selected device is still transitioning or failed to transition, the operation can target the wrong device. Model and checksum validation of the original selection do not prove the eventual flashing transport is that same device. Depending on the firmware/reset choice this can destroy data or leave a device unusable.

**Narrow correction:** Capture and validate the selected physical USB identity before reboot, reject pre-existing or ambiguous download-mode candidates, and require the same attachment to transition and remain selected until flashing starts. Use only a selector actually supported by the installed packaged samloader; do not invent a flag or add a source build. If reliable binding cannot be established, fail closed and require an explicit physically isolated single-device workflow. Preserve all current confirmations and firmware checks.

**Reason / benefit:** The device actually modified is the device the operator selected and confirmed, including across USB mode changes.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Static call/data-flow through selection, reboot, USB enumeration and flash command. Required isolated transport fixtures: second same-model device already in download mode; selected device never returns; USB disconnect/replacement between detection and flash. No real flashing was performed.

**Source excerpt - [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/lib/perl5/site_perl/labwc-adb/AndroidADB/Vendor/Samsung.pm`](#file-287), L400-426:**

```text

 401      my ($self) = @_;
 402      print 'Waiting up to '
 403          . $self->config->samsung_download_wait_seconds
 404          . " seconds for Samsung Download Mode.\n";
 405      my $status = $self->command->run_signal(
 406          'TERM',
 407          5,
 408          $self->config->samsung_download_wait_seconds,
 409          $self->config->require_tool(
 410              'samloader',
 411              'samloader-rs is not installed',
 412          ),
 413          '--usb-backend',
 414          'nusb',
 415          'detect',
 416          '--wait',
 417      );
 418      $status == 0
 419          or fail('samloader did not detect a supported Samsung Download Mode device');
 420  
 421      my $count = $self->_count_download_devices;
 422      require_value(

 424          "exactly one supported Samsung Download Mode device is required; found $count",
 425      );
 426      return;
```


<a id="f11"></a>
### F11 - Standalone nftables generation leaves new persistent files in place after validation or reload failure

**Severity:** Medium. **Classification:** Confirmed standalone generator recovery gap; distinct from the desktop firewall transaction.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/sbin/nft-policy-generate.py`](#file-217).

**Evidence and control flow:** nft-policy-generate.py:1787-1796 writes each generated configuration before :1798-1805 runs nft -c. At :1807-1814 reload can also fail. The PolicyError handler :1829-1831 returns 2 without restoring the previous generation. Optional backup_existing creates copies but is not rollback. The separate labwc_firewall/nftables.py:86-136 desktop path does restore disk/live state; this finding must not be attributed to that path.

**Impact and limits:** A root administrator using --write --check, or a failed installation/configuration step, can leave invalid or partly published persistent rules even though the currently loaded kernel rules remain unchanged. A later restart/reboot then consumes those failed artifacts. Reload timeouts also leave live-versus-disk state uncertain.

**Narrow correction:** Keep the existing renderer and flags, but stage a complete generation for validation before publication and retain the previous files through successful validation/reload. Restore both persistent state and, when reload may have applied, the previous live policy; retain recovery material on rollback failure. Validate option combinations before writing. Reuse the existing desktop transaction concepts without merging unrelated policy engines.

**Reason / benefit:** A rejected policy cannot unexpectedly become the next boot policy; uncertain reload state has a recoverable previous generation.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Source ordering and error-handler inspection; no nftables invocation or live policy change. Required isolated fixtures: nft -c rejects output, a middle file write fails, reload times out after applying, rollback fails, and --reload without --check. Assert exact previous bytes or an explicit retained recovery bundle.

**Source excerpt - [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/sbin/nft-policy-generate.py`](#file-217), L1787-1806:**

```text
1787          if args.write:
1788              if args.backup or as_bool(safety.get("backup_before_apply"), False):
1789                  backup_dir = map_to_target_root(args.backup_dir, args.target_root) if args.backup_dir.is_absolute() else args.backup_dir
1790                  backup_path = backup_existing(list(rendered.keys()), backup_dir)
1791                  if backup_path:
1792                      eprint(f"backup: {backup_path}")
1793              for path, content in rendered.items():
1794                  mode = 0o0755 if path.name == "nftables.conf" else 0o0644
1795                  atomic_write(path, content, mode=mode)
1796                  eprint(f"wrote: {path}")
1797  
1798          if args.check:
1799              if not args.write:
1800                  raise PolicyError("--check requires --write so nft can read generated include files")
1801              conf_path = paths["nftables_conf"]
1802              nft_bin = resolve_executable("nft", "/usr/sbin/nft")
1803              run_checked([nft_bin, "-c", "-f", str(conf_path)], "nft validation", timeout_seconds=args.command_timeout)
1804              eprint("nft validation: ok")
```

<a id="f12"></a>
### F12 - SSH copy wrappers misinterpret IPv6 hosts and ambiguous local pathnames

**Severity:** Low. **Classification:** Confirmed argument-formatting defect; no SSH connection made.

**Source/integration scope:** [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/bin/xssh-send`](#file-208); [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/bin/xssh-retrieve`](#file-207).

**Evidence and control flow:** Both validate_host functions accept colons, but xssh-send:54 and xssh-retrieve:53 construct user@host:path without IPv6 brackets. Local operands are passed unchanged; an existing relative name such as host:file contains no slash before its colon and is parsed by scp as a remote specification, not a local file. These are argument-formatting issues despite correct shell quoting. [S8], [S9]

**Impact and limits:** Accepted IPv6 literals do not reach the intended host. Colon-bearing local filenames can cause an unintended additional remote connection or a failed/incorrect transfer. Normal DNS/IPv4 hosts and unambiguous local paths are unaffected; this is not shell injection.

**Narrow correction:** Format validated colon-containing host literals with brackets, and make local operands explicitly local by using an absolute path or a ./ prefix for relative names. Preserve current SSH host-key verification, SFTP defaults, quoted argv and port checks; do not enable legacy SCP or disable host-key checking.

**Reason / benefit:** Accepted host and pathname syntax maps to the intended transfer endpoints without changing SSH trust defaults.

**Verification status and acceptance:** Source operand construction plus OpenSSH scp documentation and the primary OpenSSH colon() parser. Required command-capture fixtures: DNS, IPv4, IPv6, scoped IPv6, relative colon-bearing filenames, spaces, leading dash and missing operands. No network transfer was executed.

**Source excerpt - [`d-i/forky/hooks/target/usr/local/bin/xssh-send`](#file-208), L51-54:**

